newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks record fresh gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks record fresh gains at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks followed through on their recent strength to close higher Monday, driven by a new surge on Wall Street and a favorable local trading environment, dealers said.
"The prevailing good mood was boosted by the IMF's support for fiscal policy, while foreign markets provided an ideal framework for more gains here," said broker Emilio Alessandro.
International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus arrived in Buenos Aires Sunday and endorsed fiscal reform plans.
The MerVal index .MERV rose 1.2 percent Monday to 538.49, stretching gains so far this month to 5.8 percent.
But traders noted deals were becoming more selective.
"The pace of trading was slower today and buyers were more careful, although many continued to favor the oil sector which has spearheaded the market's recovery," said Alessandro.
Oil stocks were boosted first by rising world crude prices and then by news Thursday night of planned leadership changes in giant YPF, the bolsa bellwether.
In the session winners bashed losers 40 to 16 and 13 issues closed unchanged.
The broad market index matched MerVal gains of 1.2 percent in floor volume of 21.1 million pesos, compared to Friday's healthy tally of 26.7 million Friday -- the highest in five weeks.
Over-the-counter volume picked up to a moderately strong 100.3 million pesos from 88.3 million Friday.
Best MerVal performers in the session were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Juan Minetti and Banco Frances, which jumped 6.6 percent, 4.4 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively.

The day's heaviest main-tier loser was petrochemical concern Ipako, which continued eroding a recent surge triggered by news of its merger with holding company Garovaglio. Ipako, which will be absorbed by Garovaglio in the deal, closed off 2.8 percent.
Other blue-chip losers were carmaker Sevel and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which shed 1.4 percent and 1.2 percent, respectively.
